L-glessner-finish-2226
      Plain brick joints and gate member grain
      
    
    
    Ticket
    T-2226.
    Sources
    habs_glessner_house_il_1015_drawings, wlemay_glessner_courtyard_2024_159537051, owner_glessner_v4_reconstruction_brief_2026. Previously flat stair returns and Light stair, pier and boundary faces receive an original half-bond surface study using the existing courtyard clay, mortar and numeric course schedule. The 215.9 by 66.675 mm course module, 9 mm joint, 5 mm normal-map recess, 2 mm edge transition and restrained per-unit kiln distribution are reconstructed, not a measured 1904 material sample. The texture repeats after eight bricks and thirty-two courses. Individually modeled brick faces retain their existing geometry and fabric: the extra joints apply only to plain masonry. No photograph pixels, tracings or imported texture are used. Rear-gate ledges and braces receive grain along their own timber axis, at the existing physical oak texture scale. Cut ends retain a generic original oak study on a noncollapsed mapping; their growth rings are not measured or simulated. Joint positions, supports, contacts, hardware and silhouettes remain the existing reconstruction. Full and Light use the same new material library; the simplified tier does not acquire additional geometry. Neutral-light diagnostics distinguish the scene's blue shade from the owner-approved grey-greige granite. They are capture-only observations, not a historical colour calibration or a change to July lighting. Existing dark glazing and restrained material roughness remain. No new directional dirt map, orange iron rust, modern copper patina or neglected mid-century decay is invented for the seventeen-year-old house. The separately cited family typescript remains a textual comparison with its unresolved rights unchanged; these new assets derive only from original project textures, numeric construction and cleared references. Exact period weathering is still unmeasured.
